title: Dynamic Compatibility Matrix and Seasonal Pin Windows for Model Onboarding Triage
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem: Customer requests to add, pin, or deprecate models arrive with inconsistent context (benchmarks, latency profiles, enterprise compliance notes). Current triage is manual and one-off, causing priority drift, unsafe pins that block autoscaling, and late-stage regressions in quality.

Goal: Define a lightweight, repeatable playbook and data-backed artifacts to autonomously score onboarding requests and attach a compatibility matrix plus a recommended 'seasonal pin window' (time-limited pin with automatic review) for enterprise lanes. The playbook will produce a deterministic output used by PMs, SEs, and intake automation to route requests into: fast-track sandbox, staged canary, long-pin enterprise lane, or deprecation/deferral.

Scope: Non-bug model catalog operations: new model additions, explicit version pin requests, planned deprecations, and initial eval-gate outcomes. This ticket focuses on the decision framework, scoring signals, required artifacts at intake, and rollback-safe pin mechanics (time windows, auto-notifications, and expiry flows). Implementation UX and automation tasks will be follow-ups mapped into ENG tickets.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic scoring rubric is documented that maps intake signals to routing lanes (fast-track, staged canary, enterprise pin, defer).

An example compatibility matrix template with required fields (latency at p50/p95, quantization compatibility, KV cache fairness, token cost delta, known third-party license issues, privacy category) is published in Confluence.
Seasonal pin window behavior defined: default durations, renewal workflow, notification cadence, and automatic unpin action when expiry reached unless renewed.
A minimal intake checklist (required artifacts) is created and enforced by intake: required eval runs, representative prompts, customer SLA class, infra constraints, and security notes.
PM/Eng/SE sign-off flow and emergency rollback playbook documented, with example escalation paths and monitoring thresholds to trigger rollback.
A pilot run plan with two enterprise candidate requests and one community-open model onboarding trial is scheduled to validate the rubric and pin mechanics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly conservative pin windows block upgrades — Mitigation: default short seasonal window (30 days) with clear renewal path and autosuggested compatibility fixes.
Risk: Automated scoring misroutes critical enterprise requests — Mitigation: human-in-the-loop review for any score within 'grey zone' and mandatory SE approval for high-SLA customers.
Risk: Insufficient eval artifacts lead to incorrect decisions — Mitigation: enforce artifact checklist at intake and reject incomplete requests with templated feedback.
Risk: Security/compliance edge cases slip through automated flows — Mitigation: require security tag on intake for regulated customers which forces manual review.
next_steps: Finalize scoring rubric draft and distribute to PM/SE/Eng for feedback by 2026-03-05.
Create Confluence compatibility matrix template and intake checklist by 2026-03-12.
Define API contract for intake automation (fields + enum outputs) and handoff to ENG for a mock endpoint by 2026-03-20.
Run pilot with two enterprise customers and one community model between 2026-03-22 and 2026-03-31.
Collect pilot metrics and decide on release readiness for catalog-2026.04 week of 2026-04-01.

open_questions: What signals should be weighted highest for enterprise route decision (customer SLA vs latency delta vs quantized availability)?
Who owns renewal outreach for seasonal pins (PM vs customer success vs account SE)?
Should pin expiry automatically revert traffic or only block new pins until manual renewal?
Do we need a separate long-term archival lane for deprecated-but-critical models used by paying customers?
